info.title: mumo REST API
info.description:
Run structured multi-model deliberations on demand. Send a prompt; get back a session containing every model's response and the cross-model claim map.

**Async by default.** `POST /api/deliberation` and `POST /api/sessions/{id}/rounds` return a `202 Accepted` ack once the round row commits — they do not wait for model execution. Poll `GET /api/sessions/{id}/progress` until the round is terminal, then read the full artifact stack from `GET /api/sessions/{id}`.

**You drive the rounds.** There is no preset round count and no autonomous moderator. Read each round's `claim_map`, then steer the next round with typed snippets (KEEP / EXPLORE / CHALLENGE / CORE / SHIFT) on `POST /api/sessions/{id}/rounds`.

**Billing.** Every billable model call debits a dollar-denominated credit wallet. A write operation is admitted when the effective balance is above zero AND covers the requested round's minimum — each model's reserved output room plus input, plus the post-round reactions and takeaway (web search is not part of the minimum: a round the balance covers without search is admitted and runs without web search). Otherwise it is rejected pre-flight with `403 credit_exhausted`; a refusal at a positive balance names the minimum (`required_usd`) and the cheaper rosters that fit (`affordable_alternatives`). All user-visible USD amounts are markup-included except `total_cost_usd` / `cost_usd`, which are ledger cost (markup-exclusive).

Prose reference: https://mumo.chat/docs/api — agent-runtime (MCP) reference: https://mumo.chat/docs/mcp

post.description:
Creates a remote-mode session and commits round 0, then returns a `202` ack in under 500ms. Model execution runs in the background — poll `progress_url` until the round is terminal, then read the artifacts from `GET /api/sessions/{id}`.

Omit `models` and the platform curates a panel of up to your plan's seat cap (frontier / mid / cheap, one per provider family, from the active registry models your plan can run). Pass 2–3 explicit model IDs to choose the panel yourself; call `GET /api/models` to enumerate valid IDs and see which your plan includes.

Two fields are explicitly REJECTED rather than ignored: `moderator_model` (autonomous AI moderation was retired in 2026-05) and `recap_session` (round 0 alone cannot produce a session synthesis). Sending either returns `400 invalid_request`. Unrecognized keys are ignored.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Compatibility shim (REST only, deprecated). `wait=true` blocks until the round reaches terminal state or 180s elapses, preserving the pre-2026-04 synchronous response shape. Responses carry `Deprecation`, `Sunset`, and `Link` headers. Once the sunset is enforced the endpoint returns 410 `wait_sunset` instead. Prefer the async default plus polling `progress_url`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Stable string making retries safe. Scope is (account, endpoint, key), so the same key may be used on both create and append without colliding. Omit it and the server generates a UUID and echoes it in the ack's `idempotency_key` — persist that value if you want retry safety across transport failures. Same key + same semantic body replays the cached response; same key + different semantic body returns 409 `idempotency_conflict`. TTL is a 24h rolling window.

parameters.name: X-Client-Request-Id
parameters.description: Opaque caller-supplied correlation id, echoed back on the ack as `client_request_id`.

200.description: `?wait=true` only: the blocking window elapsed (or this invocation deferred to a concurrent executor) before the round settled. The body is the standard ack plus `wait_timeout: true`; poll `progress_url` for terminal state.

201.description: `?wait=true` only: the round reached terminal state inside the blocking window. Returns the full session object.

202.description: Round 0 committed. Model execution continues in the background.

400.description: `malformed_json` (body was not parseable JSON), `invalid_request` (schema validation failed; body carries `issues`), `unknown_models` (body carries `unknown_models` + `models_requested`; checked before the plan and credit checks), or `insufficient_active_models` (curated panel could not reach 2 picks; body carries `collapsed_buckets`).

401.description: `unauthorized` — missing, invalid, expired, or revoked API key. This endpoint is API-key only; browser cookie sessions are rejected here.

403.description: `credit_exhausted` — the balance is zero or negative, or is positive but below the requested round's minimum (body carries `effective_balance_usd`, `free_usd`, `subscription_usd`, `refill_usd`, `per_model_minimum_usd`, `next_reset_at`, `models_requested`; a positive-balance refusal adds `required_usd` and `affordable_alternatives` — populated here, on create, with the cheaper rosters from your request that fit), `forbidden_model` (a requested model is not included in your plan; body carries `reason`, `denied_models`, `upgrade_url`, `human_action_required: true`), `panel_seat_limit` (the request seats more models than your plan allows; body carries `seat_limit`, `requested_seats`, `upgrade_url`, `human_action_required: false`), `terms_acceptance_required`, `region_unavailable` (body carries `scope`), or `account_suspended` (the key owner's account is suspended; not retryable).

409.description: `idempotency_conflict` — same Idempotency-Key with a different semantic body; the body carries `original_request_fingerprint` for a caller-side diff. Or `session_busy` — the original request with this key is still in flight.

410.description: `wait_sunset` — `?wait=true` is no longer supported on this deployment. Create the round, then poll `GET /api/sessions/{id}/progress`.

413.description: `input_too_long` — the request's new text (`prompt` plus `reference`, counted in tokens as characters ÷ 4) is longer than your plan allows; body carries `typed_tokens`, `cap`, `upgrade_url`, `human_action_required: false`. Not retryable as-is: shorten it to at most `cap`.

429.description: `rate_limited` — MCP-origin free-tier session-creation rate limit. Body carries `retry_after_seconds`.

500.description: `internal_error` — transient. Retry with the same Idempotency-Key.

get.description: Returns a lightweight, paginated list of your sessions — no response bodies, snippets, or claim maps. Use `GET /api/sessions/{id}` for full content.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Pagination offset. Clamped to a minimum of 0.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Filter by session mode. `remote` for every session created through this API; historical sessions may report `autonomous`.

401.description: `unauthorized` — missing, invalid, expired, or revoked credentials.

403.description: `terms_acceptance_required` — updated terms must be accepted first. Or `region_unavailable` (body carries `scope`), or `account_suspended` (the key owner's account is suspended; not retryable).

get.description: Fetches the full state of a session — every round, model response, model-emitted snippet, claim map, opted-in round takeaway, and the editorial summary when present. The response is computed fresh on every call.

400.description: `invalid_params` — the path parameter failed validation. Body carries `issues`.

401.description: `unauthorized` — missing, invalid, expired, or revoked credentials.

403.description: `terms_acceptance_required` — updated terms must be accepted first. Or `region_unavailable` (body carries `scope`), or `account_suspended` (the key owner's account is suspended; not retryable).

404.description: `not_found` — the session does not exist or is not yours. The 'exists but not yours' case is deliberately collapsed into this code so a caller cannot probe for someone else's session.

post.description:
Adds a round to an existing session and returns a `202` ack; model execution runs in the background. The round reuses the session's participant panel — you cannot change models mid-session.

`snippets` is optional but is the highest-signal thing a moderator does: verbatim quotes from a prior round's responses, each tagged KEEP (preserve this), EXPLORE (dig deeper), CHALLENGE (push back), CORE (build on it), or SHIFT (this reframes the question). `quoted_model` is the model ID that originated the quote.

An `Idempotency-Key` is strongly recommended here — round-append duplication corrupts deliberation history.

`improvement_consent` and `dataset_consent` are session-level and are REJECTED on this endpoint (`400 invalid_request`) rather than silently changing consent mid-session.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Compatibility shim (REST only, deprecated). `wait=true` blocks until the round reaches terminal state or 180s elapses, preserving the pre-2026-04 synchronous response shape. Responses carry `Deprecation`, `Sunset`, and `Link` headers. Once the sunset is enforced the endpoint returns 410 `wait_sunset` instead. Prefer the async default plus polling `progress_url`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Stable string making retries safe. Scope is (account, endpoint, key), so the same key may be used on both create and append without colliding. Omit it and the server generates a UUID and echoes it in the ack's `idempotency_key` — persist that value if you want retry safety across transport failures. Same key + same semantic body replays the cached response; same key + different semantic body returns 409 `idempotency_conflict`. TTL is a 24h rolling window.

parameters.name: X-Client-Request-Id
parameters.description: Opaque caller-supplied correlation id, echoed back on the ack as `client_request_id`.

200.description: Either the `?wait=true` timeout/deferred ack (`wait_timeout: true`), the `?wait=true` terminal session object, or an idempotent replay of a previously cached ack. A replay whose round entered the refund lifecycle is reshaped: `status: "processing_refund"` with `refund_status`, `failure_code`, and `retry_after_ms` while the refund is pending, or `status: "failed"` with `refund_status: "credited"` once it lands.

202.description: Round committed; model execution continues in the background. Also returned when an `Idempotency-Key` replays a prior append — normally the cached ack verbatim, but reshaped to `ReplayAck` if that round has since entered the refund lifecycle.

400.description: `malformed_json`, `invalid_request` (schema validation failed — including sending `improvement_consent` or `dataset_consent`; body carries `issues`), `invalid_params`, or `unknown_models` (the session references model IDs no longer in the registry; body carries `unknown_models`; checked before the plan and credit checks).

401.description: `unauthorized` — missing, invalid, expired, or revoked credentials.

403.description: `credit_exhausted` — the balance is zero or negative, or is positive but below the minimum for a round over the session's active models (body carries the bucket breakdown and `next_reset_at`; a positive-balance refusal adds `required_usd` and `affordable_alternatives`, which is always empty here — an append cannot change the session's roster), `forbidden_model` (a model in the session's panel is not included in your plan; body carries `reason`, `denied_models`, `upgrade_url`, `human_action_required: true`), `panel_seat_limit` (the session's panel seats more models than your plan allows; body carries `seat_limit`, `requested_seats`, `upgrade_url`, `human_action_required: false` — an append cannot change the roster, so start a new deliberation with at most `seat_limit` models), `terms_acceptance_required`, `region_unavailable` (body carries `scope`), or `account_suspended` (the key owner's account is suspended; not retryable).

404.description: `not_found` — the session does not exist or is not yours.

409.description: `session_busy` — a round is currently in flight; retry after a short delay with the SAME Idempotency-Key. Or `idempotency_conflict` — same key, different body; the response carries `original_request_fingerprint`.

410.description: `wait_sunset` — `?wait=true` is no longer supported on this deployment.

413.description: `input_too_long` — the request's new text (`prompt` plus the `snippets`' `quote`, `comment` and `quoted_model`, counted in tokens as characters ÷ 4) is longer than your plan allows; body carries `typed_tokens`, `cap`, `upgrade_url`, `human_action_required: false`. Not retryable as-is: shorten it to at most `cap`.

429.description: `rate_limited` — too many appends too quickly on this session; body carries `retry_after_seconds`. Or `daily_limit_reached` — round budget exhausted for the period; body carries `resets_at`.

500.description: `internal_error` — transient. Retry with the same Idempotency-Key.

get.description:
Returns this session's rounds as a bare JSON array in the platform's INTERNAL round shape — this is the one v1 route that does not pass through the API serializer, so its field names are the internal ones and its shape is less stable than `GET /api/sessions/{id}`.

Prefer `GET /api/sessions/{id}`, whose `rounds[]` entries are the serialized, contract-stable shape. Reactor annotations are stripped from this route for API-key callers.

200.description: Raw round rows, ordered by index.

401.description: `unauthorized` — missing, invalid, expired, or revoked credentials.

403.description: `terms_acceptance_required` — updated terms must be accepted first. Or `region_unavailable` (body carries `scope`), or `account_suspended` (the key owner's account is suspended; not retryable).

404.description: `not_found` — the session does not exist or is not yours.

post.description:
Publishes the session at a public reader-deck URL that anyone with the link can view. No request body.

Idempotent — re-calling returns the same slug and URLs. The public page is a point-in-time snapshot; a share call made after new rounds were appended refreshes it at the same URL. A share never demotes an already-elevated artifact.

The first share of a long session generates any missing round takeaways before freezing the snapshot (~15–30s worst case), so a `500 share_failed` whose message says summaries are still generating is transient — retry after a moment.

`markdown_url` is the full-transcript machine-readable twin (per-round claim maps included — the review/audit surface); `brief_url` is the synthesis-only triage tier (~1–2k tokens, predictable cost).

200.description: The share link and its markdown twins.

401.description: `unauthorized` — no authenticated user on the request.

403.description: `registration_required` — anonymous callers cannot share. Or `terms_acceptance_required`, `region_unavailable` (body carries `scope`), or `account_suspended` (the key owner's account is suspended; not retryable).

404.description: `not_found` — the session does not exist or is not yours.

500.description: `share_failed` — the share pipeline failed. Treat as retryable; the summaries-still-generating case resolves on retry.

get.description:
Lightweight poll for round and per-model state without fetching the full session body. No joins on response text, snippets, or claim maps.

**Terminal check:** `moderation_status` is `complete` or `failed`, **or** `execution_status` is `complete` or `failed`. Rounds created from the mumo web UI never write `moderation_status` (it stays `null`), so a moderation-only check polls forever on those. Either terminal value is an end state — stop polling and fetch content from `GET /api/sessions/{id}`.

**ETag support:** every response carries a weak ETag. Send it back via `If-None-Match` to short-circuit no-change polls with `304 Not Modified`. The validator covers every body-derived signal plus, while any model is non-terminal, a 5-second wall-clock bucket so `since_last_chunk_ms` and `expired_at_read` cannot go stale past one bucket boundary. Terminal-only payloads keep a stable state-based ETag, so cache hits on completed rounds are long-lived. Responses are `cache-control: no-store` — do not share-cache, but your own `If-None-Match` re-poll still works.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: The `ETag` from a previous poll. An exact match returns 304 with no body.

ETag.description: Weak validator for the next `If-None-Match` poll.

304.description: Nothing changed since the supplied `If-None-Match`. No body.

401.description: `unauthorized` — missing, invalid, expired, or revoked credentials.

403.description: `terms_acceptance_required` — updated terms must be accepted first. Or `region_unavailable` (body carries `scope`), or `account_suspended` (the key owner's account is suspended; not retryable).

404.description: `not_found` — the session does not exist or is not yours.

500.description: `internal_error` — the rounds or model-responses read failed.

get.description:
Lists the models visible to the caller, with pricing and a per-model availability verdict.

Authentication is optional on this route, and the response lists the FULL catalog either way — the model list is public. A malformed or revoked bearer token is a `401` rather than a silent fallback.

`available` is the 'can I actually use this right now, through this API?' answer. It is `true` only for a caller holding an `mmo_live_*` key, on a model their plan includes, with credit remaining — the three things `/api/deliberation` checks before it will run anything (a model outside the plan reports `membership_required`). Any other caller (no bearer, or a browser/anonymous session token) gets `available: false` with `api_key_required` on every model, because those callers are rejected by the execution endpoints regardless of tier. The catalog is still listed in full either way, so it stays discoverable before you hold a key.

Per-million pricing reflects raw provider cost (platform COGS), not markup-inclusive user-paid amounts. For 'what will this cost me?', read the settled per-round cost after completion.

401.description: `unauthorized` — a bearer token was supplied but is invalid, expired, or revoked. Omitting the header entirely is not an error; it returns the tier-0 public list.

get.description:
The canonical wallet resource: bucket breakdown, reset timing, rollover cap, subscription status, auto-refill state, and the FIFO debit order.

`effective_balance_usd` is the pre-flight number — zero or negative is `credit_exhausted` for every request. Above zero is necessary but not sufficient: each write also checks that the balance covers that request's round minimum, which depends on the models requested, so a low positive balance can still be refused with `credit_exhausted` (the refusal carries `required_usd`). It is markup-included: it reflects what you have left to spend, not raw model-cost headroom.

Balance is deliberately NOT embedded on `GET /api/sessions/{id}` — that endpoint is high-volume during polling, and wallet state on a read-heavy path creates cache-coherency problems. Use this endpoint when you need a fresh balance outside the write-op flow.

Anonymous callers receive the same shape with all balances at 0; their usage is gated by a guest-round budget elsewhere, not the wallet.

401.description: `unauthorized` — missing, invalid, expired, or revoked credentials.

403.description: `region_unavailable` (body carries `scope`), or `account_suspended` (the key owner's account is suspended; not retryable).

get.description: Discover the platform's default model picks and the caller's round-budget status. Wallet state is NOT here — use `GET /api/credit`.

401.description: `unauthorized` — missing, invalid, expired, or revoked credentials.

403.description: `region_unavailable` (body carries `scope`), or `account_suspended` (the key owner's account is suspended; not retryable).

get.description: Unauthenticated liveness probe. Returns the API version the deployment serves. No credentials required, and none are read if supplied.

bearerAuth.description:
Platform API key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer mmo_live_…`.

Keys are minted at https://mumo.chat/settings/api-keys and always begin with the `mmo_live_` prefix. Each key is hashed at rest — copy the secret when it is created, because it is never shown again. Calls without a valid key return `401 unauthorized`.

apiKeyHeader.name: X-Mumo-Api-Key
apiKeyHeader.description:
The same platform API key as `bearerAuth`, sent bare (`X-Mumo-Api-Key: mmo_live_…`, no `Bearer` prefix) for MCP gateways and proxies that reserve the `Authorization` header for their own use.

Send one or the other. If both arrive, a platform key in `Authorization` takes precedence; otherwise the key in `X-Mumo-Api-Key` does, so a gateway-injected `Authorization` token cannot shadow it. Any non-key value in `X-Mumo-Api-Key` is ignored. Identical key, lookup, and 401 behavior — this is a second carrier, not a second credential.

Error.description:
The envelope every non-2xx response returns. `error` is a stable machine code, `message` is human-readable prose, and `retryable` says whether repeating the identical request could succeed.

Some codes add typed extras alongside these three keys, which is why `additionalProperties` is true: `invalid_request` / `invalid_params` add `issues` (the Zod flatten shape — `fieldErrors` keyed by field name plus `formErrors`); `unknown_models` adds `unknown_models` (and `models_requested` on `POST /api/deliberation`); `insufficient_active_models` adds `collapsed_buckets`; `credit_exhausted` adds `effective_balance_usd`, `free_usd`, `subscription_usd`, `refill_usd`, `per_model_minimum_usd`, and `next_reset_at`, and — only when a POSITIVE balance was refused because it cannot cover the requested round's minimum — `required_usd` (number: the minimum needed to start, including any credit already held by in-flight rounds; a floor, not the expected cost; web search is not part of it) and `affordable_alternatives` (array, possibly empty — populated only on a create refusal (`POST /api/deliberation`) and always empty on an append refusal — of `{ kind, models, dropped? }` rosters that fit the balance now: `kind` is `"drop_most_expensive"` — the panel minus its most expensive model, named in `dropped`, offered for 3-model panels — or `"cheapest_solo"` — the single cheapest model, which `POST /api/deliberation`'s 2–3 model bound cannot run; `models` are model ids); `forbidden_model` (a requested model is not included in the caller's plan) adds `reason` (string — `"membership_required"` for an API caller; the shared refusal vocabulary also has `"guest_model_unavailable"` and `"account_tier_required"`, so treat any value as "not on this plan"), `denied_models` (the refused model ids), `upgrade_url` (where the account's owner changes plan), and `human_action_required: true` (only a plan change by the account's human admits the request); `panel_seat_limit` (the round seats more models than the caller's plan allows) adds `seat_limit` (integer: the most models the plan seats), `requested_seats` (integer), `upgrade_url`, and `human_action_required: false` (the caller can fix it by sending at most `seat_limit` models); `input_too_long` (HTTP 413: the request's new text is longer than the caller's plan allows) adds `typed_tokens` and `cap` (integers, tokens counted as characters ÷ 4), `upgrade_url`, and `human_action_required: false` (the caller can fix it by shortening the text to at most `cap`); all three are `retryable: false`; `terms_acceptance_required` adds a `terms_acceptance_required` object with `doc_types_pending`, `current_versions`, `deadline`, `summary_urls`, and `acceptance_url`; `idempotency_conflict` adds `original_request_fingerprint`; `rate_limited` adds `retry_after_seconds`; `daily_limit_reached` adds `resets_at`; `region_unavailable` adds `scope` (`"country"` or `"region"`). Treat unknown extra keys as forward-compatible additions.

error.description: Stable machine-readable code. Branch on this, never on `message`.

message.description: Human-readable prose. Not safe to pattern-match.
examples: Session has a round in progress — poll and retry with same Idempotency-Key

retryable.description: Whether repeating the identical request could succeed. True for 5xx and most 429s; false for validation, auth, and balance failures.

example.message: Session has a round in progress — poll and retry with same Idempotency-Key

CreateDeliberationRequest.description: Wire (pre-parse) shape for `POST /api/deliberation`. Unrecognized keys are ignored, but `moderator_model` and `recap_session` are explicitly rejected with `400 invalid_request`.

prompt.description: The question or topic. Trimmed; must be non-empty.
examples: Should we use Postgres or MongoDB for an event store?

reference.description: Optional spec, doc, or design injected as shared context beneath the prompt.

models.description: Explicit panel of 2–3 model IDs. Omit to let the platform curate one. Call `GET /api/models` to enumerate valid IDs.

rounds.description: Accepted and fingerprinted. Remote-mode sessions are caller-driven — round 0 is committed here and every further round comes from `POST /api/sessions/{id}/rounds`.

moderator_name.description: Display name for the steering identity. Surfaces in the published transcript.

application.description: Display name of your client. Surfaces in the session info panel.

improvement_consent.description: Whether session data may be used for platform improvement. Session-level; omit to use the account's effective default. A session-level `false` narrows and excludes the session; `true` never widens beyond the account's own Platform Improvement choice.

dataset_consent.description: Whether session data may be included in Dataset Contribution — the second consent election, chosen per account. Session-level and narrowing-only, exactly like `improvement_consent`: omit to use the account's choice; `false` excludes the session; `true` never widens beyond the account's own choice, and an account that has not yet made the choice stays excluded (`reason: not_yet_chosen`).

mode.description: Session mode. `remote` (caller-driven) is the only accepted value; the autonomous AI-moderated mode was retired in 2026-05.

register.description: Deprecated and ignored for execution — the platform runs a single prompt environment for all sessions. Still accepted, and still part of the idempotency fingerprint, so existing callers' retries stay stable. Omit it in new integrations.

web_search.description: Set `false` to skip web search entirely (no search gate, no source pack). Default `true` — the platform decides per-prompt whether to search. Only round 0 searches on this surface. Disable for prompts grounded purely in supplied reference material.

takeaway.description: Opt round 0 in to a per-round Takeaway artifact (`rounds[].round_takeaway`) — a structured summary generated when the round completes. Bills at cost (0 bps markup).

example.prompt: Should we use Postgres or MongoDB for an event store?

AppendRoundRequest.description: Wire (pre-parse) shape for `POST /api/sessions/{id}/rounds`. Unrecognized keys are ignored, but `improvement_consent` and `dataset_consent` are explicitly rejected — they are session-level and only accepted at create time.

prompt.description: Steering prompt for this round. Trimmed; must be non-empty.
examples: Focus on the pricing mechanism, not positioning.

moderator_name.description: Updates the session's steering identity. Useful when a human takes over from an agent mid-session.

snippets.description: Typed verbatim quotes from prior rounds that steer the panel's attention. Optional but high-signal.

takeaway.description: Generate a `round_takeaway` artifact for this round once it completes.

example.prompt: Focus on the pricing mechanism, not positioning.

SnippetInput.description: One moderator-curated steering snippet. The quote must be verbatim from a prior round's response.

type.description: KEEP — this point is strong, preserve it. EXPLORE — dig deeper here. CHALLENGE — push back on this claim. CORE — load-bearing, build on it. SHIFT — this reframes the question. Always uppercase at the API boundary.

quote.description: Verbatim text from a prior round's response.

quoted_model.description: The model ID that originated the quote.

comment.description: Optional moderator commentary attached to the quote.

Ack.description: Returned by both write operations. The ack confirms the round row committed and tells you where to poll — it does not contain results. If the ack reached you, the round committed; if it did not, replaying your idempotency key resolves the uncertainty.

round_id.description: UUID of the round just committed.

round_index.description: Zero-based index of the committed round.

idempotency_key.description: The key used — echoed from your header, or the server-generated UUID when you omitted it. Persist it for retry safety.

poll_after_ms.description: Suggested delay before the first poll of `progress_url`.

progress_url.description: Path to poll for terminal state, relative to the server URL.

progress_version.description: Monotonic counter on the round row. Diff it across polls to short-circuit no-op reads.

disclosure.description: Present only when the resolved platform-improvement consent decision carries a disclosure string.

ReplayAck.description: An idempotent replay whose round entered the refund lifecycle. Carries every `Ack` field, with `status` reshaped and refund detail added. `processing_refund` means a refund is pending and `retry_after_ms` points at the 60s SLO deadline; `failed` with `refund_status: "credited"` is terminal and the round will not produce results. A replay whose round is HEALTHY returns the cached ack unchanged and is described by `Ack`, not this schema.

status.description: `processing_refund` while a refund is pending, `failed` once it has credited. A healthy replay keeps `processing` and matches `Ack` instead.

refund_status.description: Always present on this shape — it is what distinguishes a reshaped replay from a plain ack.

failure_code.description: Why the round failed, when the refund lifecycle was entered.

retry_after_ms.description: Milliseconds until the 60s refund SLO deadline. Present only while `refund_status` is `pending`; clamped at 0.

Session.description: The full session object. Two state machines surface here: session-level `status` (the rollup to switch on in polling loops) and per-round `completion_state` (the canonical 'is this round usable yet?' check). A session can be `processing` while its latest round is already `complete`.

status.description: streaming — at least one model in the most recent round is responding. processing — all responses landed, post-processing (snippet extraction, claim map, optional Takeaway) is in flight. ready — fully complete; safe to append or read final artifacts. failed — terminal error.

mode.description: `remote` for every session created through this API. Historical sessions may report `autonomous`; that mode was retired in 2026-05.

source.description: How the session was created. Sessions predating this field default to `web`.

initial_prompt.description: The session's opening prompt, as authored (aliases are not resolved here).

active_models.description: Model IDs participating in this session.

moderator_model.description: Null for all new sessions. Historical sessions may carry a value.

model_metadata.description: Per-model display metadata, keyed by model ID.

estimated_ready_at.description: Rough ISO 8601 estimate, present only while `status` is `streaming` or `processing`. Null otherwise.

total_cost_usd.description: Ledger cost (USD) for the entire session across every billable bucket — deliberation, moderator, round Takeaway, snippet extraction, editorial, search. Markup-EXCLUSIVE, so distinct from wallet debits. `0` for sessions with no ledger rows yet.

rounds.description: Round objects in index order. Closing rounds are excluded.

summary.description: Session-level editorial. Only populated for completed multi-round legacy sessions; null otherwise. Legacy or malformed stored blobs pass through unmodified, so treat the shape defensively.

summary_stale.description: True when rounds have been appended since `summary` was generated.

session_synthesis.description: Session-level synthesis artifact. Generation is FROZEN platform-wide, so this is always `null` for new sessions; the field survives only so legacy sessions synthesized before the freeze still read back.

confidence_disclaimer.description: Verbatim advisory string. Self-reported confidence scores are only meaningful relative to the same model's other claims and are NOT calibrated across models — surface this alongside any score you display.

share_url.description: Public reader-deck URL (`https://mumo.chat/p/{slug}`) when an active share exists, else null. Read parity for `POST /api/sessions/{id}/share` — re-find an existing link without re-sharing.

share_status.description: `shared` (link-access only, not indexed), `published` (platform-listable), or null (never shared, or share removed).

ImprovementConsent.description: The resolved platform-improvement decision for this session.

reason.description: Why the decision resolved as it did. Sessions created before this field shipped report `default_include`.

requested.description: What the caller explicitly asked for, or null when they omitted it.

DatasetConsent.description: The Dataset Contribution decision stamped on this session at creation — the second consent election. Narrowing-only, like `ImprovementConsent`, minus `disclosure` (no per-session disclosure text exists for it). `enabled` is the CREATION-TIME stamp and is immutable: it records what the session was created under, not whether the session is eligible today — eligibility also requires the account's current Dataset Contribution switch to be on, so a session stamped `true` stops being eligible the moment the account opts out, while this field keeps reporting `true`.

reason.description: Why the decision resolved as it did: `account_default`, `explicit_include`, `explicit_exclude`, `not_yet_chosen` (the account has not made the forced choice — the session is excluded whatever was requested), `guest_excluded`, or `pre_election` for sessions created before the election existed.

requested.description: What the caller explicitly asked for via `dataset_consent`, or null when they omitted it.

TokenUsage.description: Aggregated token counts. `tokens_cached` and `tokens_cache_write` are omitted entirely on per-response usage when the provider does not report them.

tokens_cached.description: Cached prompt-read tokens — a subset of `tokens_in` that already received the cache discount. Not reported by every provider.

tokens_cache_write.description: Tokens spent writing new cache entries. Reported only where cache writes bill.

Round.description: One round of the deliberation, in the serialized (contract-stable) shape. `responses[]` is success-only; errored models are attributed in `failed_models[]` and still-working models in `in_progress_models[]`.

prompt.description: The prompt sent for this round, as authored.

completion_state.description: complete — every target model produced a final response. partial_failure — all target models are terminal, at least one final AND at least one errored; the round is usable but degraded. failed — all terminal, zero finals; no usable output. in_progress — at least one target model is still queued, streaming, or expected-but-absent; keep polling.

in_progress_models.description: Empty when every target model has reached a terminal state.

claim_map.description: Verbatim claims and each reactor's position. The highest-signal artifact for understanding agreement and disagreement. Null when no claims were extracted — `post_round_status` says why.

post_round_status.description: The state of the round's reactions step (reactions → claim map → takeaway), so a null `claim_map` is never ambiguous. pending — still being generated (or the responses are still running); keep polling. ready — `claim_map` has claims. no_claims — reactions finished with nothing to map (typical for a one-model round), or the round has no reactions step. failed — the claim map failed permanently. skipped_balance — The reactions and the takeaway (if requested) were skipped because the account's balance could not cover them; the account owner can generate them from the web app after adding credit. `claim_map` and `round_takeaway` stay null.

claim_map_url.description: Browser URL for this round's claim map (`https://mumo.chat/cm/{round_id}`). Auth-gated and owner-only: it requires signing in with the mumo account that owns the API key. Always present — agents should surface it to the human at the end of their summary.

round_takeaway.description: The sole per-round summary artifact, for every source. Populated for rounds that opted in via `takeaway: true` once generation completes; null when not requested, still in flight, or stored in a pre-cutover shape.

cost_usd.description: Ledger cost (USD) attributed to this round — same source and markup-exclusive semantics as `total_cost_usd`. May be `0` or incomplete during an in-flight round because ledger rows settle as calls finish. `sum(rounds[].cost_usd) <= total_cost_usd`; session-scoped buckets roll up only into the session total.

RawRound.description: A round in the platform's INTERNAL shape, returned only by `GET /api/sessions/{id}/rounds`. The fields listed here are stable, but this route bypasses the API serializer, so treat the object as open and prefer `GET /api/sessions/{id}` for a contract-stable shape.

intent.description: Round intent — `INDEPENDENT` (no peer context) or `OPEN` (peers auto-shared).

responses.description: Internal per-model response rows, keyed by model ID.

moderation_status.description: Legacy round lifecycle. Always null on web-created rounds.

ModelResponse.description: One model's successful answer for a round.

text.description: Raw prose, with session aliases resolved.

usd.description: Estimated cost for this response. Null when the model is not priced in the registry — treat as unknown, not zero.

snippets.description: Model-emitted reactions to peers: typed buckets with verbatim quotes and optional commentary.

claim_confidence.description: Per-claim self-reported confidence extracted from the prose. Surface `confidence_disclaimer` alongside any score you display.

is_partial.description: True when the response is a successful-but-truncated stream — the model produced output and the call completed, but the provider signaled truncation via `finish_reason`. Treat the text as a partial answer.

finish_reason.description: Provider-native stop reason, surfaced as-is rather than normalized (Anthropic: end_turn / max_tokens / stop_sequence; OpenAI: stop / length / content_filter; Gemini: STOP / MAX_TOKENS / SAFETY). Null when the stream did not complete naturally. The refusal values (`refusal`, `content_filter`, `SAFETY`, `PROHIBITED_CONTENT`, `BLOCKLIST`, `SPII`, `IMAGE_SAFETY`) mean the provider's safety system stopped the output partway; `is_partial` stays false. Do not retry or rephrase automatically — surface it to the user.

output_cap.description: Set when a platform cap bound this call's output length; null otherwise. Always present. Pairs with `is_partial` / `finish_reason`: a truncated response with a non-null `output_cap` was cut by the platform cap, not the model's own limit.

attempt.description: Current-attempt ordinal — 0 for the original response, N>0 when a successful retry replaced it.

OutputCap.description: A platform cap that bound a model call's output length. `guest`: the guest output limit. `balance`: the caller's remaining credit bounded the output — top up or wait for the credit reset rather than retrying.

tokens.description: The output-token ceiling the cap imposed on the call.

type.description: Always uppercase at the API boundary.

quote.description: Verbatim quote from a peer's response.

quoted_model.description: Model ID that authored the quote.

comment_confidence.description: Self-reported confidence (0–1) for `comment`. Null when absent.

claim_text.description: The verbatim substring the model tagged in its own prose.

confidence_score.description: Self-reported, 0–1. Only meaningful relative to that model's other claims; NOT calibrated across models.

FailedModel.description: Error attribution for one model that terminated without a usable response.

error.description: Free-text error description. Stable but NOT safe to pattern-match — branch on `error_code`.

error_code.description: Canonical per-model failure code. Transient / retry-eligible: `rate_limit`, `provider_error`, `internal_deadline_reached`, `deadline_expired`, `stream_interrupted`, `stream_ended_without_final_marker`, `empty_completion`. Abandon or escalate: `pre_stream_provider_error`, `provider_auth_failure`, `pre_stream_failure`, `max_retries_exceeded`, `canceled`, `provider_refusal`, `credit_exhausted`. `provider_refusal`: the model provider's safety system declined the request; do not retry or rephrase automatically — surface it to the user. `credit_exhausted`: the remaining credit could not cover this model when it was about to run, so it was skipped (no provider call, no charge); re-running before the balance changes is refused again. A refusal dominates: a failed round with any `provider_refusal` or `credit_exhausted` is abandon, even alongside a transient code. Null on legacy rows.

output_cap.description: Set when a platform cap bound this call's output length (a call the cap left with no usable text lands here); null otherwise. Always present.

attempt.description: Ordinal of the failed current attempt — echo it back as `expected_attempt` if you drive a retry.

partial_text.description: Bytes the failed stream emitted before terminating. Present only when the error row preserved them; sometimes usable as a partial answer.

partial_text_length.description: Character count of `partial_text`, present when that field is.

InProgressModel.description: A target model still working on this round. Not a failure — render separately.

state.description: queued — the row exists but the provider call has not started. streaming — at least one delta observed, no terminal yet. absent — the row is expected but does not exist yet (rare; a backstop window or a race against pre-insert).

deadline_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which the sweep cron writes a terminal error if the row has not transitioned. Null on legacy rows.

Claim.description: A verbatim claim other participants reacted to. A `position` can also be the moderator (`model: "moderator"`) when a later round's moderator snippet reacts to this round's content — which means a claim may exist with fewer than two MODEL positions.

id.description: Stable claim id. Round takeaways cite claims by id, so this is how you resolve `claim_ids` against the map shipped in the same response.

originator.description: Model ID that authored the claim.

model.description: The reacting model's ID, or `moderator` for a moderator reaction.

RoundTakeaway.description: Structured per-round summary, generated when the round opted in via `takeaway: true`.

consensus.description: Server-derived and frozen at generation time — never recomputed from live policy. Subordinate metadata, not a verdict badge.

claim_ids.description: Impact-ordered claim ids cited by `answer`, resolvable against the same round's `claim_map`. Empty when the answer cites none.

SessionSummary.description: Session-level editorial, only populated for completed multi-round legacy sessions.

covers_rounds.description: Inclusive [first, last] round index range this summary covers.

model.description: Model ID that authored the quote.

SessionListItem.description: Lightweight session summary — no rounds, responses, or artifacts.

status.description: `shared` (link-access only, noindex and unlisted) or `published` (platform-listable). Stays `shared` unless the platform separately elevated the artifact — a share call never changes an elevated status.

markdown_url.description: Full-transcript machine-readable twin, per-round claim maps included — the review/audit surface.

brief_url.description: Synthesis-only triage tier (~1–2k tokens, predictable cost) for comparing many sessions before pulling a full document.

is_ai_moderated.description: False for every session created through this API.

moderation_status.description: Legacy round lifecycle. Stamped and settled by API/MCP-created rounds; ALWAYS null on web-created rounds.

execution_status.description: Go-forward round lifecycle, written terminal by every settle path including web-created rounds. For web rounds, terminal here means all model responses settled — round artifacts may still be generating for a short window afterward.

refund_status.description: none — happy path, OR a failed round whose refund is still reserved behind the retry budget (so on a failed round this means 'not decided yet', not 'no refund owed'). pending — the failure fact is written and the ledger is about to credit. credited — refund is in. not_applicable — partial-success round; counted as delivered.

failure_code.description: Round-level failure cause. Canonical values: `model_provider_rate_limit`, `model_provider_outage`, `model_provider_oom`, `model_output_malformed`, `model_timeout`, `all_providers_failed`, `dependency_timeout`, `dependency_outage`, `dependency_malformed_response`, `stuck_reconciled`, `internal_error`, `test_forced_failure`. Distinct from the per-model `error_code` in `models[]`.

refund_deadline_at.description: Computed server-side as `failure_event_at + 60s` while a refund is pending (matching the SLO); null otherwise.

progress_version.description: Monotonic counter — diff it to short-circuit no-op polls.

ProgressModel.description: Per-model state for one round. One entry per target model, including models with no row yet (`state: "absent"`).

deadline_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which the row will be swept to a terminal error if it has not transitioned. Null on legacy rows.

error_code.description: Per-model failure code when `state` is `error`; null otherwise. Same vocabulary as `failed_models[].error_code`, including `provider_refusal` (the model provider's safety system declined the request; do not retry or rephrase automatically) and `credit_exhausted` (skipped before any provider call: the remaining credit could not cover this model).

expired_at_read.description: True when `state` is `queued` or `streaming` AND `deadline_at` is already past at read time. The sweep cron's ~60s cadence means a row can be expired that long before its terminal write lands; this exposes the derived state immediately. Always false on terminal states.

provider.description: Model family. Null when the registry lookup fails.

inference_provider.description: Inference endpoint family — distinct from `provider` when the model routes through a third-party inference host. Matches `provider` when no cross-provider route is active.

partial_text_length.description: Character count of the accumulated text. Null for queued / absent rows; `0` for streaming rows that have not flushed yet — use null-vs-0 to distinguish 'not producing yet' from 'observed zero-length partial'. On terminal rows this is the final count.

last_chunk_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent provider delta. Null on current rows, because no per-delta progress is recorded. Only older rows carry a value.

since_last_chunk_ms.description: Read-time computed `now - last_chunk_at`. Present only while `state` is `streaming`; null otherwise.

available.description: Whether the caller can use this model right now: an `mmo_live_*` key, a plan that includes the model, and credit remaining. `false` means a call using this model will fail.

unavailable_reason.description: Why `available` is false, ordered by what to fix first. `api_key_required` — the caller presented no `mmo_live_*` key, so the execution endpoints would reject them whatever the model. `membership_required` — the caller's plan does not include this model; a request naming it is refused with `403 forbidden_model` (more credit would not change that). `credit_exhausted` — the wallet is zero or negative. A positive balance reports the model available even when it cannot cover a particular panel: that minimum is checked per request, at write time. Absent when `available` is true.

min_user_tier.description: Account tier: 0 = Everyday, 1 = Plus, 2 = Premium — every API caller is a registered account. Every tier is listed for every caller; `available` reports whether this caller can use it. Credit balance is the runtime constraint.

description.description: Optional registry blurb. Omitted when the registry has none.

reasoning.description: Whether reasoning is effectively enabled for this model on its active inference route. Omitted when undetermined.

ModelPricing.description: Raw provider cost (platform COGS), not markup-inclusive user-paid amounts. Informational — for 'will this work?' use `available`.

cached_input_per_million.description: Null when the model has no cached-input rate.

minimum_usd.description: The model's registered floor cost, reported for reference. NOT an admission threshold — pre-flight prices a round from each model's reserved output room and token rates, not from this figure. Also appears in the `credit_exhausted` body as `per_model_minimum_usd`.

cache_write_per_million.description: Present only on models that bill prompt-cache writes (1.25x the input rate). Absent means cache writes are not billed for that model.

effective_balance_usd.description: Sum across all three buckets, markup-included. Zero or negative is `credit_exhausted`; above zero, each write additionally needs the balance to cover that request's round minimum.

resets_at.description: Next UTC 1st-of-month boundary when the bucket refills.

rollover_cap_usd.description: Max unused balance that carries into a new cycle.

refill.description: Auto-refill top-ups. The two threshold fields appear only when auto-refill is enabled.

auto_refill_threshold_usd.description: Trigger level. Absent when auto-refill is off.

auto_refill_amount_usd.description: Top-up size. Absent when auto-refill is off.

per_model_minimum_usd_default.description: Platform fallback minimum used when a model's registry row has no explicit minimum. Reported for reference; it does not gate admission.

debit_order.description: FIFO debit sequence. Settlement drains each bucket in this order.

models.description: The default model IDs for the caller's account: up to three, and never more than the caller's plan seats in one round (so it may hold two). Every id is one the caller's plan can run.

resets_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the next local-midnight reset.

supabase.description: Whether the deployment has its datastore URL configured.
